A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LatentChem and contain 34 readable pages, including complete Appendices A–J. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the scientific content and presentation.

before.justification: v1 reports original LatentChem benchmark results, component ablations, latent-budget experiments, noise interventions, and case studies in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, latent-dynamics analyses, and case studies reported in v1.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices C–D retain the same ChemAdapter, ChemUpdater, Latent Projector, latent reasoning loop, training stages, and objectives.

E1.justification: The training corpus and evaluated coverage of ChemCoTBench, Mol-Instructions, ChEBI-20, and ChemLLMBench are unchanged. No tasks or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding tables: Qwen-3-8B variants, staged chemical models, Coconut-Chem, and the reported external-model comparisons in Appendix J are all retained.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendices D–E retain identical evaluation sample counts, model configurations, preprocessing, metrics, training budgets, and generation settings. The supplementary experimental procedures also match.

E4.justification: The component ablations, Gaussian-noise interventions, latent-budget stress tests, t-SNE/RSA analyses, and case studies are unchanged, including the supplementary evidence in Appendices G–I.

E5.justification: The sign-test procedure and p < 0.01 significance markers in Section 5.1 and Table 2 are unchanged. No repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting information is added or removed.

E6.justification: Tables 2–9 and the empirical figures retain the same result entries, numerical values, and findings. For example, Table 2 reports the same 59.88% ChemCoTBench non-tie win rate against Stage 1+2+4.

T1.justification: Appendix A retains identical definitions, assumptions, Theorem A.9, proof, and efficiency derivations. The architecture and training-loss equations also remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about spontaneous CoT internalization, the advantages of continuous latent reasoning, benchmark performance, and efficiency.

C2.justification: The interpretations of causal necessity, compensatory textual reasoning, and preserved chemical topology are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitation concerning inaccessible human-readable intermediate reasoning and the same future directions.

D1.justification: The dataset snapshot disclosure, implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and code-access link are unchanged. Appendices C–E contain no added or revised reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 54 references are unchanged. The positioning relative to chemical LLMs, Coconut, and other latent-reasoning approaches is retained.

P1.justification: The first-page attribution changes from Hypo Sciences Reasoning Team to Haven, and dates are updated. Section 7 separately identifies Xiangru Tang as Corresponding Author rather than listing him among Co-Authors. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the Hypo Sciences logo with Haven branding, changes blue document accents and links to dark gray, and adds a corresponding-author block on page 13. Scientific figures, tables, captions, and their placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revision changes branding, colors, dates, and author-role presentation while retaining all scientific content and evidence, including the appendices. Explicitly identifying the corresponding author provides a small administrative clarification, but these edits do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
